text: Every Thursday before sunrise the square behind the old railway station fills with vans.

The number 14 bus will run every twenty minutes instead of every half hour from the first of next month. The first departure from the depot moves forward to ten past five, and the last one back from the hospital leaves at a quarter past eleven. Printed timetables are available from the driver.

The indoor pool closes for two weeks in September so that the tiles around the deep end can be replaced. Season tickets will be extended by the same number of days. During the closure, swimming lessons for the primary schools move to the pool in the neighbouring town.

Street lamps along the river path have been fitted with new bulbs that use a third of the electricity. They are dimmed to half strength between midnight and five in the morning and return to full brightness when a walker or cyclist comes within thirty metres.

Allotment holders are reminded that bonfires are allowed only on the first Saturday of the month and never before four in the afternoon. Green waste can be left at the gate on Fridays, where it is collected and shredded for the shared compost bays.

The lost property office at the town hall holds eleven umbrellas, four single gloves, a child's scooter and a set of false teeth handed in after the summer fair. Items not claimed within three months are passed to the charity shop on the high street.

Road gritting begins when the forecast shows a road temperature below one degree. The main routes and the hill up to the hospital are treated first, the bus routes second and the side streets only if the cold lasts more than three days. Salt bins on steep corners are refilled each November.

The volunteer fire brigade is looking for six new members. No experience is needed. Training takes place on Tuesday evenings at the station behind the cattle market and lasts about a year before a recruit goes out on a first call.

The school crossing on the mill road will have a patrol again from Monday. A warden will be on duty from eight until nine in the morning and from three until four in the afternoon during term time. Drivers are asked to keep the zigzag lines clear.

The town band rehearses in the scout hut every Thursday at half past seven and welcomes players of any standard. Cornets and a tuba can be lent to beginners. The summer programme includes four concerts on the bandstand and the parade at the harvest festival.

Brown bins for garden waste will be emptied weekly from April until the end of October. Grass cuttings, leaves and small branches are accepted. Soil, stones and kitchen scraps are not, and a bin that contains them will be left with a tag on the handle.

The footbridge by the weir is closed until further notice after the spring flood loosened two of its planks. Walkers should cross at the road bridge four hundred metres upstream. Repairs are expected to take three weeks once the water level has dropped.

The Saturday morning market has two free pitches following the retirement of the fishmonger. Applications from traders selling fresh food are preferred. Forms can be collected from the market office, which is the green hut beside the public weighbridge.
